import itertools,json
assign=list(itertools.product(range(4),repeat=3)); edges=((0,1),(1,2),(0,2)); charge=(1,2,1); moved=(0,2,2)
def div(q):
 r=[0,0,0]
 for a,(x,y) in zip(q,edges):r[x]+=a;r[y]-=a
 return tuple(a%4 for a in r)
si=[div(q)==charge for q in assign]; sf=[div(q)==moved for q in assign]
assert sum(si)==sum(sf)==4
# Amplitudes are integer numerators over2; use true orthogonal tree projection.
ti=[int(ok and q[2]==0) for ok,q in zip(si,assign)]; ci=[int(ok)-t for ok,t in zip(si,ti)]

def shift(v):
 out=[0]*64
 for q,a in zip(assign,v):out[assign.index((q[0],q[1],(q[2]-1)%4))]=a
 return out
def dot(a,b):return sum(x*y for x,y in zip(a,b))
parts={'TT':dot(tf,shift(ti)),'TC':dot(tf,shift(ci)),'CT':dot(cf,shift(ti)),'CC':dot(cf,shift(ci))}
assert parts==dict(TT=0,TC=1,CT=1,CC=2)
# Fourier numerator: full amplitude has denominator16, phases exact Gaussian integers.
nonflat_num2=0
for z in assign:
 val=sum((1j**(sum(qj*zj for qj,zj in zip(q,z))%4) for q,ok in zip(assign,si) if ok),0j)
 if (z[0]+z[1]-z[2])%4:nonflat_num2+=int(val.real)**2+int(val.imag)**2
assert nonflat_num2==0
